headline: AI voice fraud outruns every defense, leading to $893M in reported losses in 2025
summary: AI-powered voice cloning scams led to over $893 million in reported losses in 2025, with older adults being the primary target. These sophisticated attacks are often undetectable by victims.
details: Sharon Brightwell lost $15,000 to an AI-cloned voice of her daughter, believing she was bailing her out of jail. This incident highlights how advanced AI fraud can target ordinary individuals effectively.

This type of fraud, requiring frontier machine learning, is now a common crime in the US, perpetrated at scale for minimal cost. Law enforcement and financial institutions have struggled to contain the problem for two years.

The FBI's 2026 report categorized AI-enabled fraud separately for the first time, logging over 22,000 complaints and $893 million in adjusted losses for 2025. Victims aged 60 and over accounted for $352 million of this sum.
These FBI figures are considered an understatement, as many victims never realize AI was involved in the scam. The true scale of AI-enabled financial crime is likely much larger than reported.

Globally, INTERPOL estimated financial fraud losses at $442 billion in 2025, describing an "industrialization of fraud." AI-enhanced fraud is reportedly 4.5 times more profitable than traditional methods, with agentic AI systems capable of autonomous campaigns.

headline: Apple closed a popular workaround for buying an unlocked iPhone with carrier financing
summary: Apple has officially ended a method that allowed customers to purchase unlocked iPhones while still utilizing carrier financing options. This change impacts how many users acquire their devices.
details: Apple has officially terminated a widely-used method that enabled customers to acquire an unlocked iPhone through carrier financing plans. This workaround allowed users to bypass carrier locking while still benefiting from installment payment options.

The policy adjustment means that customers seeking an unlocked iPhone will now likely need to purchase it outright at full price directly from Apple or authorized retailers. This change aims to streamline purchase processes and potentially reduce complexities associated with carrier agreements.
caption:
A popular method to get an unlocked iPhone with carrier financing has been shut down by Apple. This affects how many users acquire their new devices.

The policy adjustment means that customers seeking an unlocked iPhone will now likely need to purchase it outright at full price directly from Apple or authorized retailers. This change aims to streamline purchase processes and potentially reduce complexities associated with carrier agreements.
